SURGO × UNIVERSITY OF MANITOBA · SENEGAL

Demand, services and modern contraceptive use

Updated département-only supply assignment. Supply summaries use confirmed FP providers (s5_6 = 1), valid values by measure, and no facility weights. Daily provision replaces counseling; cleaned stockout burden replaces popular-product stock. Stockout burden is reversed to continuity before scoring. Health beliefs use PB2A alone. Main geographic classifications compare final average-z scores with zero. Every woman receives the average recorded facility characteristics of her own département. Her personal demand responses remain individual; Rural/Urban residence is retained as an adjustment variable.

Joint evidence helps planners see where reported concerns accompany service weaknesses. The models estimate adjusted associations, while the map identifies relative patterns of service weaknesses and reported concerns. They do not establish causal binding constraints or the budget share to allocate to either side.

01 · COVERAGE AND LINKAGE

Women and facilities overlap in 33 départements

The join retains all 7,169 original women. Manitoba contains 2,043 facility records across 46 départements. Of these, 1,648 facilities in 33 départements overlap with SURGO; 395 facilities are in 13 départements without surveyed women. This map shows all source facility records before FP-provider restriction and all source women before selecting the need group. The updated supply analyses below use 1,568 confirmed FP providers in the 33 linked départements.

02 · USE, INTENTION AND METHOD CHOICE

Among women SURGO classifies as in need of family planning

Population used from this section onward: original SURGO FPN2 = 1, exactly as recorded in the source survey. This gives 1,905 women. No older script’s need_n recoding or sterilization/hysterectomy additions are applied. Eleven nonconsenting records are outside estimation and have FPN2 = 95.

Every bar and sub-bar has the same denominator: all 1,905 women with FPN2 = 1. Percentages use WEIGHT; n is an unweighted respondent count. Capped whiskers are 95% logit intervals using the available RB0H census-district design, constructed before domain selection. Original sampling strata and finite-population corrections are unavailable. Subsets overlap: modern users are included in current users, so these bars do not sum to 100%. 4 users have unresolved modern/traditional classification; 98 have another or unresolved initiation-preference response. *Preference concerns the method wanted at initiation; the type of alternative wanted is not established. Future intention concerns any method, without a specified 12-month initiation window.

Initial pattern. Weighted current use is 50.4%, including 45.9% modern use. Another 17.1% are nonusers with intention and 32.3% nonusers without stated intention. These groups help distinguish existing use from stated future interest without treating this cross-sectional survey as a transition study.

Département planning profiles · z-score average

How the scores and thresholds work
  1. Summarize départements. Calculate six weighted concern percentages among women in need and six unweighted supply summaries using valid facility responses.
  2. Align direction before calculation. Retain the five higher-is-better supply measures. Convert stockout burden to stock continuity = 1 − burden. For example, 40% burden becomes 60% continuity. The heatmap retains the original burden percentage. All six scoring inputs now have higher = stronger provision.
  3. Standardize each component across the 33 départements. Use (département value − component mean) ÷ component sample SD. Each département contributes equally to these reference values.
  4. Average within each side. Average six demand z-scores and six favorable-supply z-scores. Higher demand means more concern; higher favorable supply means stronger recorded provision. Supply risk is the negative of readiness: higher burden lowers readiness and raises risk. This equals first reversing the other five measures to risks, retaining burden as a risk, and averaging their standardized scores. Each component has mean zero; their average also has mean zero, but its SD is not necessarily one. A score of +0.2 is an average of standardized component values, not 20 percentage points.
  5. Compare the final scores with their mean: zero. Flag demand above 0 and favorable supply readiness below 0. Scores equal to zero within numerical tolerance remain unflagged. Every component is centered across the same 33 départements, so the mean of each final average-z score is zero.

Why this construction? Standardization gives components comparable dispersion and equal averaging makes the chosen weights explicit. The OECD/JRC handbook describes these composite-indicator methods; it does not endorse our particular variables or zero threshold. Correlated components, extreme values and sparse responses can affect the result. Each département has equal weight in the reference, so zero is the surveyed-département average, not a national population estimate. Averaging six z-scores preserves the ranking of their sum, while keeping the scale interpretable as an average standardized component.

These are relative planning categories. “Neither flagged” does not establish adequate services or absence of barriers. The map’s contextual demand score is separate from the personal demand score used in models. Alternative scoring methods are shown in the appendix.

Both: 9Demand only: 10Supply only: 6Neither flagged: 8Facility data only: 13

Planning signal. Of 33 départements, 9 have both sides flagged, 10 demand only, 6 supply only, and 8 neither. Use the component comparisons to identify what warrants investigation; the category is not a causal diagnosis.

† Fewer than 50 unweighted women in need; 4 départements have fewer than 25. Small samples and incomplete facility coverage can make rankings unstable. Hover over the map for weighted CPR and mCPR.

Which service weaknesses and reported concerns recur across départements?

Both-flagged départements are included on each flagged side. The supply and demand groups therefore overlap. A département contributes to three components, so percentages do not sum to 100%. These are relative component patterns, not service-standard failures. Each supply measure uses its own valid-response denominator. Daily provision is defined for 1,560 of 1,568 FP facilities; 8 have no recorded offered category and remain undefined. Stockout burden is higher = worse, whereas the other five raw supply percentages are higher = better.

Short- and long-acting options together means at least one long-acting and three short-acting categories at the same facility. Free provision and training average within-facility proportions; they are not shares of facilities offering any free product or having any trained provider. The confidence indicator is unchanged: it measures confidence choosing a method or managing side effects, not objective knowledge.

Modern use in relation to personal concerns and local services

All models: 1,558 women with original SURGO FPN2 = 1, including 795 modern users across 33 départements. Outcome: current modern use = 1; confirmed traditional-only use or nonuse = 0. Score assigned to each womanConstructionObserved model variation

Supply risk scoreStandardize her assigned 6 département-wide measures against the fixed 33-département planning means/SDs. Average and reverse the sign: higher = weaker provision.33 distinct numeric scores across 33 départements. Rural and Urban women in one département receive the same score.

Key finding. In Model 3, the demand odds ratio is 0.27 (0.20–0.35) and the supply risk odds ratio 0.72 (0.38–1.36) per one original average-z index point. The demand association remains after accounting for recorded supply and covariates. The supply interval includes 1, so its independent association remains uncertain. These do not allocate a percentage of nonuse to either side.

Planning interpretation. The curves show how predicted modern use varies with each score for the same women, holding other predictors at their observed values. Their levels and uncertainty are easier to interpret than odds ratios. They are adjusted cross-sectional comparisons, not expected gains from removing barriers. An uncertain supply slope does not establish adequate services.

Which reported concerns accompany lower use?

Models 4 and 5 retain personal responses separately. Model 5 also includes the same contextual supply score. The supply-only model is Model 2, shown again for reference.

Key finding. In Model 5, opposition to family planning has OR 0.12 (0.06–0.21); anticipated stigma has OR 0.57 (0.41–0.80). The six demand coefficients are jointly associated with use (Holm p <0.001). Use the heatmap to locate these concerns alongside service weaknesses; these associations do not establish which intervention would be most effective.

What this means for planning. The adjusted present-versus-absent difference is -41.4 percentage points for opposition and -11.1 points for anticipated stigma. The model predicts the same women under each response setting, retains their supply and other characteristics, and averages using WEIGHT. These gaps identify patterns to investigate; they are not intervention-effect estimates.

DEFINITIONS AND VERIFICATION

Measures, denominators and interpretation

Six demand domains: questions and missing-response rules
IndicatorSource and interpretation
Healthcare permission barriersHS7C: 1 = permission to seek a doctor is a challenge; 2 = no. General healthcare permission, not FP-specific partner approval.
Anticipated social stigmaPB7B/C: 1/2 on either item, concerning being seen by someone known or what people would say. Zero requires both valid negatives (3/4); unresolved responses remain missing unless the other item establishes concern.
Health / side-effect beliefsPB2A only: 1/2 = health problems are very/somewhat likely; 3/4 = unlikely. Other answers remain unresolved. PB2B/C are excluded. This measures perceived health harm, not experienced side effects.
Future-fertility concernsAny MP4_a–f selected for later childbearing concerns about reversible methods. Require coherent MP4_a–i 0/1 responses, at least one selection or explicit none, no none-plus-method contradiction, and MP4_99 = 0. Sterilization items MP4_g/h do not create a fertility concern; unknown responses are not zero.
Low method knowledge · retained labelMC5A/B: 3/4 on either item, measuring low confidence choosing a suitable method or handling side effects/switching. This is self-efficacy/confidence, not an objective knowledge test. Zero requires both valid 1/2 answers.
Opposes family planningFP1: 3/4 = against versus 1/2 = in favor. Unfamiliarity, no opinion and other special codes remain unresolved.

These items are not restricted to married women or current nonusers. A known positive can establish an any-concern flag. Zero requires valid negative responses on every included item; other combinations remain unresolved.

Uncertainty responses are not automatically data errors or absence of concern. Future-fertility concerns and PB2A health beliefs account for most unresolved demand values. Département heatmaps use valid-domain responses; individual models require complete predictor values.

Six supply measures and response coverage
IndicatorCalculation and interpretation
Short + long-acting offeringAverage one_larc_3_sa_offer, joined as share_offer_larc_and_3_sa. Share meeting the original ≥1 long-acting plus ≥3 short-acting product/category rule. Higher = stronger recorded provision.
Free-product provisionAverage valid facility p_free_prod proportions, joined as mean_p_free_prod. A value of 60% means the average reporting facility provides 60% of its recorded products free; it is not the percentage of facilities offering any free method.
Trained-provider shareAverage valid facility p_train proportions, joined as mean_p_train. Describes the average reporting facility’s trained-personnel proportion under the original UoM eligibility; not the share of facilities with at least one trained provider.
Daily provision of offered modern methodsFrom raw s5_7a–g: pills, injectables, male/female condoms, emergency contraception, IUD and implants. For each FP facility, count Daily (code 1) divided by categories provided Daily/Weekly/Biweekly/Monthly (codes 1–4). Code 5 Not at all is excluded from the offered denominator; unknown responses enter neither numerator nor denominator. A zero offered denominator is undefined. Average valid facility ratios as mean_daily_modern_provision. A département value of 75% means the average reporting facility provides 75% of its recorded offered modern categories daily; it is not the percentage of facilities providing all methods daily. Partial method responses remain conditional on recorded information. Higher = more frequent reported provision, not proof of adequate access.
At least one LARC in stockAverage one_larc_stockin, joined as share_stocked_1plus_larc. Share meeting the original at-least-one-long-acting-product stock rule. The three-LARC measure is constant FALSE and cannot be standardized.
Stockout burdenAverage the original cleaned p_any_stockout values among confirmed FP facilities, joined as mean_facility_any_stockout. A value of 40% means the average facility has 40% of assessed product groups classified as having current or recent stockouts; it is not 40% of facilities. Senegal history items s6_17 refer to the last three months. Product groups follow the UoM code and are not explicitly restricted to normally offered methods. Higher raw burden = worse. Preserve these values as supplied; use 1 − burden as stock continuity before scoring and PCA. Numeric completeness does not establish complete raw responses or independently validate the upstream unknown-response rules.

Every facility contributes equally when it has a valid value for the relevant indicator. Recorded zeros and FALSE flags are included. Unknown or undefined values are excluded from that indicator’s denominator. Cleaned flags can be complete even when underlying raw items are not; preserving the upstream definition does not validate every raw missing-data decision.

Population, weighting, covariates and model sample

Section 1 shows all source women. From Section 2 onward, the population is original SURGO FPN2 = 1: 1,905 women. The flag is unchanged; no historical need_n recoding or permanent-protection additions are applied. Original WEIGHT is retained.

All five primary specifications share 1,558 women, including 795 modern users; 347 women in need are excluded from these common models because outcome, demand or covariate information is unresolved. ApproachConstructionThreshold
Rank averageRank départements separately for each component, using average ranks for ties; average six ranks separately on each side.Demand above its final-score median; favorable supply below its median.
Mean percentagesAverage six component percentages separately on each side.Same strict final-score median rule.
Median/IQRFor each component, subtract its département median and divide by its IQR; average the transformed values separately by side.Same strict final-score median rule.
Median countCount components above the demand component medians, or below the favorable supply component medians.Flag at least four of six unfavorable components on either side.
Z-score average · primaryFor each component, subtract its département mean and divide by its sample SD; average six component z-scores on each side.Demand > 0; favorable supply readiness < 0. Zero is the mean of the final scores.

Median ties are unflagged. The median-count method requires a strict majority: four of six unfavorable components on either side. The rank-average, mean-percentage and Median/IQR comparisons retain separate final-score medians. The primary z-score method uses zero, its final-score mean. These classifications are relative to the linked départements, not absolute standards.

APPENDIX B · PCA SENSITIVITY

Alternative scores from the same individual and département inputs

Separate weighted PCAs use six personal demand indicators and six assigned département supply measures, including daily provision and stock continuity (1 − burden). Demand PCA uses 1,564 complete women; supply PCA uses 1,905 women across 33 département profiles. Repeated supply profiles are weighted by the summed WEIGHT of represented women; these are not facility weights.

Interpretation. Demand PC1 retains 24.8% of demand variation; supply PC1 retains 37.4%. Supply PC1 has mixed signs: Trained-provider share run opposite to the other provision components. Its negative is a supply pattern score, not uniformly ordered risk. PCA loadings describe variation in the inputs, not their association with modern use or their program importance. The equal-weight z-score remains primary.
